previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis was admitted after worsening left hip pain following a fall one week prior. Imaging confirmed left superior and inferior pubic rami fractures without displacement, managed conservatively with weight-bearing as tolerated and pain control using oxycodone. She also reported chronic abdominal pain and nausea, attributed to constipation from withholding lactulose; symptoms improved with reinitiation of her bowel regimen. Her cirrhosis remained stable without encephalopathy or decompensation. She was maintained on her home medications, including lactulose, rifaximin, spironolactone, and psychiatric drugs. Physical therapy cleared her for discharge home with a walker and home services. She was discharged with follow-up arranged in orthopedics and hepatology, advised to abstain from alcohol, and given a short course of oxycodone for pain.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen with and without contrast.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with HCV/EtOH cirrhosis and ___ s/p TACE,
admitted with N/V and abdominal pain, also due for ___ screening 3-phase CT
scan  // due for ___ 3-phase screening CT. Also please evaluate for source of
epigastric/RUQ pain

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen were acquired without
intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in detecting
vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor detection.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.
No oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  Total DLP 1226.57 mGy cm

COMPARISON:  Most recent prior CT abdomen pelvis dated ___.  Liver
ultrasound ___

FINDINGS: 

There is mild bibasilar atelectasis.  Otherwise, the lung bases are clear.

The liver has a nodular contour consistent with patient's history of
cirrhosis.  There is a large recannulated umbilical vein.  The spleen is not
enlarged.  Measuring up to 12 cm in craniocaudal dimension.  No evidence of
ascites.  There are gastric and esophageal varices.

Within segment II of the liver there is a hypodense lesion which correlates
with patient's history of prior ___ status post TS.  When compared to prior
examination there is a new arterial enhancement along half of the hypodense
lesion that washes out on delayed imaging.  The entire lesion measures 15 x 15
x15mm and the enhancing portion measures 12 x 7 x 14 mm.  The portal vein is
patent.  There is conventional hepatic arterial anatomy.

The common bile duct measures up to 10 mm in this postcholecystectomy patient
which may be patient's new baseline.

Multiple hypodense lesions in the kidneys, previously characterized as simple
cysts on prior MRCP.  Otherwise the kidneys, adrenal glands, and pancreas are
unremarkable.

The visualized bowel is grossly unremarkable.  No evidence of free air.

There is moderate atherosclerotic calcification of the abdominal aorta.  No
aneurysmal dilatation.

IMPRESSION: 

Within the region of previously diagnosed ___ status post TACE in segment II
there is a new 14 mm focus of arterial enhancement along the left margin of
the treated lesion which demonstrates washout on delayed imaging consistent
with recurrent HCC.  OPTN 5T lesion.

Cirrhosis with evidence of portal hypertension.
